title: Race Home
story: Three attackers push forward on the big goal; the instant they lose the ball, the two defenders race the other way toward two small goals before the coach's count reaches zero.
setup: Build a 30x20-yard area with a full-size goal at one end and two mini goals at the other. Three attacking bibs start in the middle third and attack the full-size goal; two defending bibs protect it. Keep spare balls beside the big goal for quick restarts.
instructions: Three attackers attack the full-size goal; two defenders protect it.
The instant the defenders win the ball, the ball goes out of play, or a shot is taken, the defenders attack either small goal at the far end.
The coach counts down aloud from five the moment the ball turns over.
The counter-attacking pair scores by finishing in a small goal before zero; the three recovering players score by winning the ball back first.
Reset at the big goal and rotate roles frequently so everyone attacks and recovers.
coach_lens: Watch the three recovering players, not the ball: do they turn and sprint the instant possession changes, or watch the ball first and lose a step? Notice their first three steps — toward the play or standing still — and whether anyone gets goal-side of the ball before challenging.
questions: What is the first thing your body should do the moment you lose the ball?

simplify: Move the small goals nearer halfway so the recovery sprint is shorter.
challenge: Drop the countdown to four seconds, or play 4v3, so the recovery window is tighter.
low_attendance: Run 2v1 with a single defender if numbers are short, keeping the same turnover-and-race trigger.
high_attendance: Duplicate the area so no group waits long between reps.
limited_equipment: Use cone gates instead of mini goals for the counter-attack targets.

safety: Keep the recovery lane clear of spectators and other groups.
Call out when a shot is taken so players near both goals stay aware of ball flight.

source.title: Trainingspraxis: Angreifen, Verteidigen und Umschalten
source.reviewer_notes: SmallSide-authored 3v2 transition game scaling win-it-score-it's immediate-counterattack idea to a small group, directly motivated by a coach's own match observation that players recover slowly after losing the ball. Informed by the same DFB transition principles as win-it-score-it; no wording or artwork translated or reproduced.
